summary: This article surveys how local school districts are funded and how they allocate budgets since the new fiscal year began on September 1, 2023. It covers property tax and state formula funding, inequality concerns, shifting spending toward STEM, technology, support services and teacher development, and links between funding and performance. It also describes innovative models like participatory budgeting and the Equity in Funding Act.
one_line: Overview of local education funding models and budget allocation trends in 2023, including equity concerns, innovative models, and links to student performance.
key_facts: The new fiscal year for the school districts discussed began on September 1, 2023.
Local education systems are typically funded through a combination of state, local, and federal resources, with property taxes a long-standing staple.
Jonathon Cartwright, superintendent of the Millfield School District, says local property taxes provide stability but can entrench inequality due to variances in property wealth.
State governments often use formulas based on enrollment numbers, local wealth, and student needs to allocate funds.
Dr. Lisa Han, an education policy analyst, says disparities persist because affluent districts can supplement state and federal funds more effectively.
As of September 10, 2023, the Brookstone District began directing a higher percentage of its budget toward STEM programs and support services for underperforming students.
A Newstead University study dated September 15, 2023 found targeted investments in early literacy programs significantly improved reading scores across participating districts.

Sarah Tilton, Director of Instruction at West Valley School District, reported on October 2, 2023 that investing in teacher professional development produced a measurable uptick in student achievement.
Jason Kim, chief financial officer of the Eastbridge District, said the district adopted participatory budgeting involving teachers and parents since late September 2023.
The Equity in Funding Act, passed on October 12, 2023, aims to address funding inequalities in historically underserved communities.
A November 5, 2023 report by the Education Resource Network indicated a national trend toward increasing the budget share for classroom technology.
Principal Amelia Vance of Jefferson Middle School said on November 10, 2023 that additional funds for after-school programs have been instrumental in improving students' academic and personal lives.
School districts are legally required to provide appropriate services to students with disabilities, which can be expensive.
